purpose: Defines the minimum machine-checkable traceability contract for the first-MVP vertical-slice delivery-planning model. It groups the accepted product-story backlog into observable, independently demonstrable outcomes. It does not create, reinterpret, or resolve any story, requirement, validation gate, or technical-baseline decision, and it grants no implementation, ADR, technical-acceptance, test, task, or execution-packet authority.

rules: A vertical slice is a bounded delivery-planning grouping of one or more accepted product stories sharing one coherent observable product/operational outcome; it is not a new requirement, story, use case, or implementation task.
Every vertical slice has at least one member story, and every member story id resolves to an id in the accepted story backlog.
Every accepted story in the backlog is assigned to exactly one vertical slice; there is no secondary or supporting membership.
actor_ids equals the exact sorted unique union of actor_id values from the slice's member stories.
dependencies resolve to other declared vertical-slice ids, are not self-referential, and form no cycle across the full slice set.

Every cross-slice STORY DEPENDS_ON STORY relationship declared in the story backlog induces a direct dependency between the two stories' containing slices; an induced dependency does not require a dependency_rationale entry.

dependency_rationale is a mapping from a target vertical-slice id already present in the same slice's own dependencies to a justification object with a non-empty rationale string and one or more source_refs entries that each resolve to a concrete accepted source id (a requirement, use case, story, or acceptance-criterion id); an entry keyed by an id absent from the slice's own dependencies is invalid and does not justify anything.

A declared dependency whose two member-story sets carry no induced STORY DEPENDS_ON STORY relationship must have a corresponding valid dependency_rationale entry for its target; the validator deterministically rejects a declared additional dependency that lacks one.

readiness_gate_ids equals the exact sorted unique union of validation-gate ids referenced (with any effect) by the requirement_links of the slice's member stories, resolved through docs/current/requirements/DOPIS_MVP_REQUIREMENTS.json validation_links; this is traceability metadata only and does not by itself flatten, resolve, or reinterpret the source requirement's BLOCK/CALIBRATE/VALIDATE status.
Every technical_baseline_refs id resolves to a decision id declared in docs/planning/DOPIS_MINIMUM_TECHNICAL_BASELINE.json.
Every deferred_baseline_decision_refs id resolves to a decision id declared in docs/planning/DOPIS_MINIMUM_TECHNICAL_BASELINE.json whose classification is DEFERRED.
No vertical-slice field may grant implementation authority or state an API, database schema, class, event topic, test case, task, file layout, or implementation algorithm.

recommended_delivery_order contains every declared vertical-slice id exactly once and is a topological order consistent with every declared hard dependency; it is planning guidance only and grants no implementation authority, release commitment, estimate, or schedule.

future_node_indexes.vertical_slices: DOPIS_TRACEABILITY_MATRIX.json future_nodes.vertical_slices is an exact validator-recomputed index of vertical-slice ids declared in DOPIS_VERTICAL_SLICES.json.
